Clement I.

[Bishop of Rome; succeeded Linus, 
A.D.
 67, or Anacletus, 91; supposed to be the Clement to whom St. Paul refers as his fellow-laborer; died, according to Eusebius, 100, and is reckoned among the martyrs.]
We are in the same boat.
To the church of Corinth, on the occasion of a dissension. The letter from which this is taken is still extant, and is prized as an important memorial of the early Church.
